summary: The design needs a stronger execution boundary between descriptor construction, persistence, and refresh. The largest risks are tenant routing, provenance enforcement, missing snapshot behavior, and parity/security across multiple executors.

suggestions.title: Centralize linked execution for publish, refresh, and HTML
suggestions.rationale: `_pin_save` and `publish_surface` currently validate and persist the envelope without executing anything, while `_refresh` only dispatches to `RecipeRunner`. Implement one linked-surface service used by both save paths and refresh, with atomic failure behavior and persisted snapshot metadata.

suggestions.title: Make TOOL provenance enforceable at persistence boundaries
suggestions.rationale: `validate_envelope` accepts an explicit `origin` and defaults to permissive TOOL semantics, but the HTTP save path and `PublishSurfaceTool` only call `CreateSurface.model_validate`. An LLM-produced or manually supplied envelope could therefore carry `parrot_data_sources` without passing the new origin gate. Use a builder-issued trusted result or require explicit provenance validation before persistence.

suggestions.title: Implement tenant-aware source identity before building descriptors
suggestions.rationale: The current `SlugCatalog` reads public `QueryModel` rows, `QuerysourceToolkit.describe_slug` and `execute_slug` have no tenant parameter, and `QuerySlugSource` constructs `QS` without tenant routing. Adding a tenant field to the descriptor alone would allow catalog lookup, execution, and public fallback to disagree. Make `(tenant, slug)` the identity for discovery, authorization, and execution, with explicit tenant propagation to QS/MultiQS.

suggestions.title: Define one normalized result shape for MultiQuery sources
suggestions.rationale: The current toolkit's `execute_slug` always constructs `QS`, while `MultiQuerySlugSource` concatenates independent slug results. The proposed `is_multiquery` descriptor requires a different dispatch path and must specify how MultiQS frame dictionaries become `rows`, columns, targets, and union inputs. Add explicit normalization rules and fixtures for public MultiQuery, unsupported tenant MultiQuery, and empty frames.

suggestions.title: Make request the canonical condition representation
suggestions.rationale: `build_conditions` currently adds `querylimit`, `_offset`, `refresh`, and forced conditions, while the proposed `request` block omits some of those fields. A descriptor can therefore contain internally consistent-looking `conditions` and `request` values that rebuild differently after a filter edit. Either make `request` complete and canonical, or mark generated fields explicitly and test serialize/rebuild round trips.

suggestions.title: Defer arbitrary ref transforms or reduce them to opaque allowlisted IDs
suggestions.rationale: An SRI hash authenticates downloaded JavaScript bytes but does not make executing catalogued JavaScript safe, and the bundled UI currently has no metadata-aware loader or transform runtime. Reuse the existing server-side registered-transformer model, or make the descriptor carry an opaque manifest ID resolved from a tightly allowlisted route with CSP and deprecation checks.

suggestions.title: Publish fixtures as a shared consumable contract
suggestions.rationale: Python golden files and the bundled UI's Vitest tests currently live in separate package trees, so merely storing linked fixtures under Python tests will not enforce renderer parity. Ship the JSON Schema and fixtures as an explicit package artifact or CI-consumed contract, then run both Python and TypeScript executors against the identical files, including null, timezone, dtype, ordering, join-collision, and empty-result cases.

suggestions.title: Bound fetch volume before pandas transforms and close QS resources
suggestions.rationale: The proposed 500-row snapshot cap is applied after execution, while descriptors can be replayed outside the toolkit's current `max_rows` path. That permits large fetches before synchronous pandas work. Additionally, `QuerySlugSource.fetch` creates a QS object without a visible `finally`/`close` block. Enforce query-side row and byte limits, bound transform complexity, move CPU-heavy work off the event loop, and close every QS instance.

suggestions.title: Specify behavior when a linked surface has no snapshot
suggestions.rationale: `bake_envelope` raises on unresolved required bindings, and the HTML negotiation service immediately renders the stored envelope without a linked executor. A `snapshot: false` chat envelope therefore cannot safely enter existing bake/render lanes unless the target is initialized, the binding is explicitly optional, or linked-aware rendering is guaranteed. Add a concrete empty/loading contract and tests for JSON, HTML, and direct chat rendering.

suggestions.title: Carry parrot_param through FilterBar lowering
suggestions.rationale: The current FilterBar schema has only `column`, `label`, `options`, and `multiple`; lowering preserves only `parrot_role` and `parrot_filter_column`, and the bundled UI treats FilterBar as unsupported. Adding `parrot_param` only to an authored descriptor will be lost or bypassed during lowering. Extend the schema, lower it into primitive metadata, and define whether the runtime consumes raw composites or lowered nodes.

suggestions.title: Prevent stale concurrent refreshes from overwriting newer snapshots
suggestions.rationale: `update_envelope` unconditionally updates a surface by ID, and the proposed renderer interval plus manual/server refresh creates concurrent writers. A slower earlier query can overwrite a newer snapshot and its `snapshot_at`. Add an optimistic version or updated-at predicate, or serialize refreshes per surface, and return a conflict/retry result.
